title: Ansel and the Vector
premise: Felix Ishikawa smuggles memories—recorded lives, black-market griefs, stolen histories—through the checkpoints of the Meridian system aboard her patched freighter, the Vector. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the flicker was a countdown signal from Kestrel's Landing, a quarantined colony Earth officially erased, and that the memory she's been carrying unknowingly for years is its dying testimony. Hunted by customs enforcer Dae-Sun Okonkwo, who is torn between duty and the truth in Felix's cargo, Felix must choose between selling the recording to the rebellion for passage or broadcasting it through Earth's last open transmission loop—a window that closes forever when the loop ends. She broadcasts it, forcing both sides to reckon with the massacre they buried; the war collapses not into peace but into a fragile, honest truce, and Felix finally stops running.
about_author: August Thornbury is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that never saw each other, an experience that haunts every page of their fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog rolls in on schedule, and where they insist the best stories are the ones someone paid to have carried quietly.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A routine smuggling run: Felix slips a widow's recorded last words past orbital customs inside a shipment of seed grain, establishing her methods, her cynicism, and her rule—never open the cargo. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking grief she won't name.

chapters.title: The Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Mid-dock at Meridian Station, gravity dies for exactly nine seconds. Coffee floats, a loader crushes a dockhand, and every screen flickers with the same coordinates: Kestrel's Landing. Felix recognizes them—from a memory canister she's carried sealed for three years. Beat: dread blooming into curiosity.

chapters.title: Cargo She Never Opened
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Alone aboard the Vector, Felix weighs her one rule against the coordinates. She cracks the old canister and finds not contraband but testimony: hours of footage from a colony Earth claims never existed, ending mid-sentence. Beat: the smuggler becomes the smuggled.

chapters.title: Inspector Okonkwo
chapters.summary: POV Dae-Sun. Customs enforcer Dae-Sun Okonkwo reviews the nine-second anomaly and flags every ship docked during it—including the Vector, whose flight pattern matches a ghost smuggler he's chased for two years. He requests a boarding. Beat: duty sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: POV alternating Felix/Dae-Sun. The inspection is a duel of manners; Dae-Sun finds nothing but memorizes everything about her. Afterward he finds a fragment of the Kestrel footage cached in a station relay—and now he knows what she's carrying. Beat: mutual recognition of equals.

chapters.title: What Kestrel Sang
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Watching the full recording, Felix learns the colony didn't die of plague as official history says—it was decommissioned, people and all, and the nine-second flicker was its automated distress beacon finally reaching full power. Beat: horror transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Buyer in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix contacts Vess, a rebellion broker offering clean papers and protection in exchange for the recording—to be used as propaganda, edited to serve the war. Felix hesitates: truth cut to fit a cause is just another lie with better production values. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant, Unsigned
chapters.summary: POV Dae-Sun. Ordered to arrest the Vector's captain on fabricated charges before she can talk, Dae-Sun digs into Kestrel's file and finds his own agency helped bury it. He stalls the warrant by six hours—an eternity, and a betrayal. Beat: the first crack in duty.

chapters.title: Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Using Dae-Sun's stolen time, Felix runs the blockade to a rebel relay station, trading her entire legitimate cargo for broadcast access she doesn't yet trust herself to use. Vess's editors begin cutting the testimony down to a weapon. Beat: complicity dawning.

chapters.title: The Edited Dead
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix watches Vess's cut: the colonists' final message stripped of its plea for accountability, reshaped to justify an imminent rebel strike on Earth's relay hub. She realizes delivering it means starting the war, not ending it. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Dae-Sun. Dae-Sun intercepts the Vector at the relay station—not to arrest Felix but because he needs to see the unedited recording himself. Armed standoff in the cargo bay resolves into two exhausted people watching the dead speak. Beat: enemies becoming witnesses together.

chapters.title: Full Testimony
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Together they watch all eleven hours: births, harvests, the evacuation order refused, the end. Dae-Sun's certainty in the institution breaks; Felix admits she took the canister years ago from a dying courier and never asked why. Beat: shared burden.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: POV Felix. They learn Earth's last open civilian transmission loop—the only channel that reaches every fleet, colony, and home without passing through military filters—shuts down permanently in four days for decommissioning. Broadcast there, unedited, the testimony cannot be suppressed. Beat: a door with a closing time.

chapters.title: Vess's Leash
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Vess discovers Felix still has the original and sends hunters; the rebel station turns hostile. Felix and Dae-Sun escape in the Vector with the canister, pursued by both fleets' patrols now. Beat: belonging nowhere, together.

chapters.title: Ghost Run
chapters.summary: POV Dae-Sun. Dae-Sun flies the evasion patterns he once used to catch her, teaching Felix his own tricks as they thread debris fields and sensor nets. In the quiet between burns, they speak honestly for the first time—about the people they failed. Beat: intimacy forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Courier's Name
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Decoding metadata in the canister, Felix identifies the dying courier who gave it to her: a Kestrel survivor's daughter who spent her last fuel finding a smuggler nobody would suspect. The message was always meant for everyone. Beat: grief given direction.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Meridian
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The only route to the loop's transmitter runs through Meridian customs, where Dae-Sun must walk back into the agency that now hunts him and forge a transit clearance while Felix hides in a grain hold like her own contraband. Beat: love tested against sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: POV Dae-Sun. The forgery works until his former partner catches him. Offered reinstatement if he surrenders Felix, Dae-Sun refuses aloud, on record, and is shot escaping. Felix gets him aboard barely alive. Beat: duty kept by breaking it—the truest form.

chapters.title: Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: POV Felix. With Dae-Sun in medical stasis and rebel and loyalist squadrons converging on the transmitter, Felix has minutes before the loop closes forever. She loads the full, unedited eleven hours and keys the broadcast. Beat: the quietest climax—her finger on one button.

chapters.title: Eleven Hours of the Dead
chapters.summary: POV multiple fleet-wide vignettes. Across the system, gunners, cooks, admirals, and children stop to listen as Kestrel's Landing speaks in its own voice, uncut. Ships power down weapons mid-approach. Some don't. Beat: the war meeting its own reflection.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The loop goes silent; the fighting sputters into ceasefire talks no one dares call peace. Felix stands trial by choice, testifying publicly, and Dae-Sun wakes to a system where his arrest report is taught in schools. Beat: justice outside the law, then inside it.

chapters.title: Vector, Bound Elsewhere
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Months later, Felix takes a legal contract ferrying Kestrel survivors home to rebuild, Dae-Sun navigating beside her. She opens her next cargo willingly: new memories, freely given, nothing to hide. Beat: belonging earned, love chosen over duty's shadow.
